title: Understanding the Problem
text: The biker is launched at an angle of $$60**\circ$$ and lands $$45.0\, \text{m}$$ away, $$20\, \text{m}$$ below the launch point. We need to find the initial speed.

title: Breaking Down the Motion
text: The motion can be broken into horizontal and vertical components. Use trigonometry to find these components.

title: Horizontal Motion
text: The horizontal distance covered is $$45.0\, \text{m}.$$ Use the formula: horizontal distance $$=$$ initial horizontal velocity × time.

title: Vertical Motion
text: The vertical motion is affected by gravity. Use the formula: vertical displacement $$=$$ initial vertical velocity × time - $$0.5$$ × $$g$$ × time².

title: Using Trigonometry
text: The initial horizontal velocity is initial speed × cos(60) and the initial vertical velocity is initial speed × sin(60).

title: Finding Time of Flight
text: Use the vertical motion equation to solve for time: $$20$$ $$=$$ initial speed × sin(60) × time - $$0.5$$ × $$9.8$$ × time².

title: Solving for Initial Speed
text: Use the horizontal motion equation: $$45$$ $$=$$ initial speed × cos(60) × time. Substitute the time found in the previous step.
